description:
1. Create a temporary workspace named "temp_test_env" to hold all intermediate files and results.  
2. Obtain the current value of the variable var from its environment and save its literal representation to "temp_test_env/var_value.txt".  
3. Inspect and record the apparent data type cues and annotations (such as surrounding quotes, sign, decimal point, or non-digit characters) into "temp_test_env/var_meta.txt".  
4. Produce a normalized string by trimming surrounding whitespace and removing any enclosing quotes from the saved representation, then write this normalized value to "temp_test_env/var_norm.txt".  
5. Attempt to interpret the normalized string as an integer; record whether the conversion succeeded, and if so the parsed integer, into "temp_test_env/parse_result.txt", and set an internal flag named "is_integer" accordingly.  
6. Based on the "is_integer" flag, prepare the single-token response ("yes" or "no") and save that token to "temp_test_env/final_answer.txt" as the prepared output for the final step.

Test if variable var is an integer? If so, tell me "yes", otherwise tell me "no". (Without quotes)
